title: Two Compasses and the Angle That Wraps: Fusing a Gyro and a Compass

questions.question: A heading estimate is 3.1 radians and a compass reads -3.1. What is the correction a filter should apply?
options: A pull of -6.2 towards the compass
A small pull of about +0.083 across the back of the circle, the short way round
questions.explanation: 3.1 and -3.1 are 0.083 apart. A filter that subtracts takes the 6.2 at its word and turns the whole way round.

questions.question: At a gain of 0.1 the plain difference gave a worst error of 3.139 radians and the short way round 0.162. What is 3.139?
options: Half a turn, as wrong as a heading can be
questions.explanation: The robot pointing straight away from where it thinks. The plain difference pulls the estimate the long way round at every crossing of the back of the circle.

questions.question: The mean of the angles 3.1 and -3.1, added and halved, is zero. What is wrong with it?
options: It is correct only for small angles
It points the opposite way from both
questions.explanation: Angles are directions, so they are averaged as unit vectors, which gives 3.142. The arithmetic mean treats an angle as a quantity on a line. The direction of the sum of the unit vectors is the right mean.

questions.question: When is the circular mean undefined?
options: When there are more than two angles
When the unit vectors cancel, as for 0 and pi
questions.explanation: There is no mean direction and returning a zero would look like a heading. The resultant has length zero and atan2 of zero and zero is not an answer. The function says so with a flag.

questions.question: The rms error fell as the gain rose from 0.005 to 0.1 and then rose again at 0.5. Why?
options: A small gain trusts the gyro and lets its bias in, and a large one trusts the compass and lets its noise in
questions.explanation: The best is in between. 0.609, 0.189, 0.048, 0.091. The best gain depends on the two sensors' errors, which is what the filter has to be told.

questions.question: Why does wrap_pi subtract the whole number of turns at once instead of looping or using atan2 of sine and cosine?
options: A loop never finishes for a very big angle and atan2 of sin and cos loses digits as the angle grows, where floor of (angle + pi) over a turn is exact for any size
questions.explanation: The test wraps angles forty and a thousand turns round and gets them back to within 1e-8.
